{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -q gpua100
#   -gpu "num=2"
#   -J "Train ResNeSt"
#   -n 1
#   -W 24:00
#   -R "rusage[mem=32GB]"
#   -o logs/%J.out
#   -e logs/%J.err

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --gpus=2 \
  --time=24h \
  --queue=gpua100 \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs

# Approximate LSF %J with Flux job id.
exec >"logs/${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"logs/${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: LSF -R "rusage[mem=32GB]" (memory request) has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J "Train ResNeSt") has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module load python3/3.7.10
module load cuda/11.5
module load cudnn
module load ffmpeg

pip3 install torch==1.9.1+cu111 torchvision==0.10.1+cu111 torchaudio==0.9.1 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html

echo "Running script..."
make train
'
"
}
